# The NIRC Cluster Graph

*Generated by `tools/cluster_graph.py` from `data/ra8424.html` (RA 8424, the 1997 NIRC base text) and `data/NIRC_section_index.csv`. Regenerate with `python -X utf8 tools/cluster_graph.py`; nothing here is hand-entered except the declaration counts in §6, which are a fixed measurement.*

## What this is

The distributed formalization design in `DEEP_RESEARCH_DISTRIBUTED_TAX_FORMALIZATION.md` §5.1 proposes partitioning the tax code by its own cross-reference graph rather than by title. This file is that partition, measured instead of assumed: every section of the NIRC, every section-level reference between them, the strongly connected components of the resulting digraph, and the resulting work frontier.

The short version: **at section granularity the graph is sparse, so the clustering is nearly a singleton partition and the frontier is wide, not deep.** Dependency order is not what limits this project. Review capacity is.

## 1. Extraction

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Sections parsed | 292 |
| Section-level edges (unique) | 163 |
| Mean out-degree | 0.56 |
| Mean in-degree | 0.56 |
| Sections with no outgoing reference | 207 |
| Sections never referenced by another section | 209 |
| Sections with neither in- nor out-edges | 169 |
| References dropped: self | 3 |
| References dropped: out of range | 0 |
| References dropped: duplicate | 36 |

Dropped references are printed deliberately. `out_of_range` is mostly references to other instruments (the Tariff and Customs Code, the Local Government Code) whose numbers collide with NIRC section numbers, and `self` is a section naming itself. Neither is a graph edge.

### Markers, and one defect worth naming

The source typesets headings as `<b>Section 24.</b>`, except §132, which is `<b>Section </b>132.` — the bold closes before the number. A strict marker regex silently loses that section and shifts every later chunk boundary. The tolerant pattern plus a strict sequence check (a marker counts only if its number is the next expected one) makes the split self-validating: if the parse ever stops at 291 sections again, the count says so.

This is a small instance of the project's central claim. A formalization pipeline is a proofreader: the extractor found a real typesetting fault in the primary source, which is exactly the class of finding Lexifina reports from doing this to Title 26.

### What counts as an edge

Only whole-section references (`Section 24`, `Sections 922 through 927`, `Secs. 24, 25 and 26`) become edges. Subdivision references — `subsection (b)`, `this Section`, `such subparagraph`, `hereof` — are counted per section as **coupling** but do not create edges, because they never leave the section. They are what makes a single section expensive, not what orders sections against each other.

| Coupling | Sections | Mean per section |
|---|---|---|
| Internal reference tokens | 321 | 1.1 |
| Sections with ≥10 internal references | 7 | — |

260 of 264 clusters are a single section. The statute's citation graph is close to a tree with a few true knots: only 32 sections sit in a cycle, and every cycle is small and local.

**The cycles.** Each is an atomic unit: formalizing any member independently would mean assuming a clause of a section you have not written yet.

## 3. Depth structure

Depth is the longest chain of unformalized dependencies beneath a cluster: depth 0 references no other section, so it can be started today; depth *k* sits on *k* dependency steps. The histogram is how far a contributor can get without waiting for anyone.

| Depth | Clusters | Sections | Units (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 208 | 209 | 328 |
| 1 | 26 | 29 | 174 |
| 2 | 7 | 15 | 97 |
| 3 | 5 | 5 | 28 |
| 4 | 4 | 20 | 263 |
| 5 | 11 | 11 | 32 |
| 6 | 3 | 3 | 5 |

Depth 0 holds 208 of 264 clusters; the deepest chain is 7 clusters. Even the worst-placed cluster waits on a handful of predecessors, not a tree — so there is no ordering reason to hold work back, only a statement-signing reason, which is the constraint §4.2 of the design document names.

The design document's title-level estimate was 90–130 formalizable sections concentrated in Titles II, III, IV, V and VII. The measure gives **113**, inside that band — but it rejects the concentration. Formalizable arithmetic turns up in every title, because assessment, limitation, penalty and allotment provisions compute too. ## 6. What this does not show

- **It is the 1997 base text.** RA 10963 and RA 11976 changed rates, thresholds and at least one cross-reference. The graph is a floor; the amended consolidated text must be re-parsed before these numbers are quoted as current law.
- **It is section granularity.** Two sections can be formally independent and still share a definition (`gross income`, `taxable income`). The shared definitions are cluster C1 in the design document, not edges here.
- **Units are text-structure estimates**, not measurements of effort. The formula rewards numbers, percentages and rule-bearing paragraphs; it cannot see that a short section is legally hard. It is checked once, below, against the seven merged sections: the aggregate holds to about 20%, individual sections are off by a factor of two in both directions, and two are wrong in kind rather than degree. Rank clusters with it; do not schedule from it.
- **Conditional references are flattened.** "If the taxpayer is a corporation, Section 27 applies" becomes a plain edge, so fan-in overstates how often a section is actually reached.

### The check on the estimate

The estimate is a text-structure heuristic with exactly one check: the seven merged sections, estimate against the Lean declarations they actually took. Declarations means def / theorem / lemma / example / structure / inductive attributable to that section in `ph-tax-code-lean/lean`, excluding the shared certificate-checker layer and the demonstration files. Attribution is a judgement call, so the counts are a one-time hand measurement recorded in `CALIBRATION`, not something this script derives from the Lean.

| Section | Units (est.) | Declarations (counted) | What was counted |
|---|---|---|---|
| §21 | 0 | 6 | Tier, classify, rank, reduced, classify_mono; the formula scores 0 |
| §24 | 14 | 30 | schedule defs, 5 monotonicity lemmas, 10 bracket examples, 8% regime |
| §109 | 12 | 11 | threshold, exemption and registration predicates, with complements |
| §116 | 3 | 3 | percentage rate, monotonicity, one example |
| §236 | 14 | 0 | no Lean declaration in this repository |
| §248 | 8 | 12 | surcharge, penalty, tiered variants, bounds |
| §249 | 7 | 8 | interest, day monotonicity, bounds |

58 estimated units against 70 counted declarations over the same seven sections. The aggregate is comfortable; the per-section errors are not, and they are not noise — they follow the text structure the formula reads. Work that is a type and its monotonicity lemmas has few numbers, so §21 scores zero; a section that is mostly procedural prose this repository has not formalized scores fourteen. The estimate ranks clusters; it does not predict what a section costs.

## 7. What follows for the roadmap

1. **Dependency order is not the bottleneck.** With 208 clusters at depth 0 and a chain of at most 7, a contributor can start almost anywhere. The scarce resource is the practitioner who signs statements, exactly as §4.2 of the design document argues.
2. **Cycles are the only real ordering constraint, and they are local.** The 4 components above should be handed to one contributor each as single assignments, never split across the desk.
3. **Fan-in is the priority signal, not section number.** Of the sections still to do, §27, §106, §22, §108, §57 are cited most and should be formalized first even though they are not the numerically first.
   §24, the most-cited section overall, is already merged — which is the reason the frontier is as wide as it is.
4. **The extractor is a deliverable.** It found a typesetting fault in the primary source on its first run. Run against the amended text it will find more, and each one is a filing against the Codification.
